name: Proxmox_VE_Cluster_Topology
description: Proxmox VE topology modelled on vSphere: cluster to node, node to guest, storage (stores, pools, disks, Ceph) and SDN networking.
technicalNotes:
The Proxmox VE map, modelled on LogicMonitor's vSphere suite so it reads the way a vSphere map does. One per cluster is enough, since it reports the whole cluster from wherever it runs.

Edges. Manage: cluster to node (a standalone host has no cluster vertex). Compute: node to guest, the edge that lets a node's alerts explain its guests'. Storage: node to each store it lists; guest to each store its disks and mount points use; store to the ZFS pool, LVM thin pool, volume group, Ceph pool or disk beneath it, thin pool to volume group, volume group and ZFS pool to their disks; node to the Ceph OSDs CRUSH places on it, OSD to its disk; and node to guest where a guest uses a host path or a passed-through device no store covers. Network: SDN only -- node to each zone it spans, zone to its VNets, VNet to each guest attached to it. Bridges, ports, bonds and VLAN interfaces are kept off the map: a bridge repeats what the Compute edge says, and a switch joins the map at the node, by the MACs on the node's resource.

Vertices, each drawn only where an instance or resource carries its key: the cluster (Proxmox_VE_Cluster_Status, Cluster); each node (its own resource, through addERI_Proxmox_VE_Node, HyperVisor); each guest (its MAC: Proxmox_VE_Cluster_GuestStatus's instance and the guest's own resource); each store (Proxmox_VE_Cluster_StorageCapacity, StorageVolume -- one per node for a local store, one for the cluster for a shared or network store); each pool (Proxmox_VE_Node_StoragePools and Proxmox_VE_Cluster_CephPools, StorageAggregate); each OSD (Proxmox_VE_Cluster_CephOSD, StorageNode); each disk (Proxmox_VE_Node_Disks, PhysicalDisk); each SDN zone and VNet (Proxmox_VE_Cluster_SDN, VirtualSwitch).

Guests are matched to their own LogicMonitor resources by the MAC of their first NIC, read from the guest config -- the identity VMware_vSphere_VirtualMachine_Topology uses; a guest with no NIC falls back to a synthesised key. Proxmox exposes no hardware identifier for a node, so each node vertex carries one synthesised key, proxmoxve--node--<node>--<ip>, with the address /cluster/status reports, which addERI_Proxmox_VE_Node stamps from the resource's system.ips; only a node with no address falls back to proxmoxve--<cluster>--<node>. Never both: the portal matches a multi-key vertex only to a resource carrying every key.

Not drawn: a node's uplink to the physical switch -- Proxmox gives no interface MAC and no LLDP; a monitored switch's own topology draws it. Guest disks as vertices of their own. Backup targets, which are a job setting, not storage a guest runs on.

Cost, hourly on one resource: a fixed handful of cluster reads (status, resources, /storage, SDN, Ceph), five or so per online node (disks, pools) and one config read per guest, through the suite's per-node breaker and time budget. A failed read leaves only its own part of the map out.

Limitation: not yet tested with the nodes of two clusters in one portal. The node key is the node's name plus its address, so two clusters whose nodes share both would be joined on the map.

Like the two addERI modules, this cannot be compiled or run outside a Collector: it works through com.logicmonitor.mod.Snippets (eriPreProcessor, generateTopology), whose output format LogicMonitor does not fully document. Every decision about an edge is made in the preamble's pveTopoPlan, which the suite's own tests run.

Applies on the cluster role (pve.cluster.role active or standby, set by the NetScan); only one of the pair prints.

Requires the PVEAuditor role: Sys.Audit on / (cluster status, node disks and Ceph), VM.Audit for the guest configs, Datastore.Audit for the stores, SDN.Audit for SDN. A guest or store the token cannot see is not drawn.
